assumptions.summary: The requested premium villa styling uses terracotta and sage rugs, a west reading lounge, dining storage, four pool loungers, a six-seat terrace table under the existing pergola, four olive trees and perimeter hedges. The pergola now uses the catalog string-lights device with a manual light slot and night-only scene state, retaining its existing placement and dimensions. Dimensions and finishes are inferred generic designs. Lawn contact is -49 mm and paved terrace contact -43 mm relative to the indoor datum, each allowing a 1 mm support gap.

The large northeast bedroom is interpreted as the requested child room; the primary suite remains the adult bedroom. A cabin bed, reading and play zones, toy storage and a colorful rug are inferred without child age or reference photos. Room identity and architecture are preserved.

No measured plan was supplied. The villa uses metre plan units with origin [0, 0], north at decreasing plan Y/front, and the garden at increasing plan Y/south. The ground shell is inferred as 24 by 18 m and the inset first floor as 20 by 16 m.

Ground walls and ceilings are inferred at 3.0 m with a 3.2 m floor-to-floor height. First-floor walls and ceilings are inferred at 2.9 m with a 3.1 m upper storey height. Exterior walls are 0.32 m and interior partitions are 0.16 m thick.

The ground floor prioritizes arrival and service rooms on the north, a central stair, a guest suite and study, and a large south-facing open kitchen/dining/living room. The first floor contains a primary suite, three additional bedrooms, a family bathroom, linen room, and central gallery landing.

The rear garden keeps broad lawn margins around a compact 17 by 3.3 m house terrace and a 12.4 by 6.2 m pool surround. The 10 by 4.2 m pool is centered behind the house. At the street side, hardscape is limited to a 5.3 by 4 m garage approach and a 1.7 by 2.8 m entry path.

The accepted demo export uses light oak in the main stair hall, open-plan living room and gallery, horizontal light oak in bedroom four, dark walnut in the primary bedroom and dressing room, square tile in the primary bathroom, and terrazzo in the central stair hall. The front driveway and entry path use limestone; terrace finishes are retained.

The accepted architecture is preserved. All eighteen interior rooms are equipped in this revision, including two connected vehicles in the double garage. No Home Assistant area, entity, credential, or binding data is encoded.

With no reference photos supplied, the 220 m² open room is inferred as a west kitchen with peninsula, a central eight-seat dining area, and an east lounge facing a 2.4 m wall-mounted television above a low media console. Furniture keeps the three south terrace sliders and the main internal passages clear.

Kitchen lighting, four pendants, wall television, speaker, floor lamp, and indoor AC use local typed slots only. The television and speaker map to separate simulated media players in the demo; household mapping remains manual. The single climate device may use unique-compatible mapping after the room is explicitly connected in the browser.

The default home includes the first-floor wraparound balcony from the supplied project export, with travertine finish and 1 m railings. Balcony access uses double white French doors at the existing south-facing window and the west-facing primary bedroom and bedroom four windows. Opening IDs and widths are retained; the 2.3 m door height is inferred.

The accepted Demo home export replaces the central stair with a 1 m wide left-turning L-shaped stair and left railing, removes the east-wall guest-bathroom window, updates room finishes and furnishings, and adds a ceiling fan, front-garden rotating sprinkler and primary-bedroom camera. Exported dimensions and positions are retained. The replacement coat rack and reading chair retain their previous repository IDs. Fan and sprinkler use local typed slots; demo simulation starts the fan at 50% speed and the sprinkler open. The camera has no simulated feed.

The requested first floor is interpreted as the ground-floor living/dining level matching the supplied coordinates and television. Added a west-wall AC between the TV and window at offset 5.3177 m, elevation 1.8898 m and depth offset 0.004 m; a pedestal fan at [13.5207, 17.5304] rotated -128.0852 degrees; and a connected floor lamp at [0.5129, 17.5525]. Catalog default dimensions and 1 mm floor support gaps are inferred. Local slots use existing demo simulation: AC starts heating, fan starts at 50%, and lamp starts on at night.
